definition: Finding anything in the shop that could cause harm (equipment, process, material, environment, behaviour).
example: Before welding, the group identified trip hazards, hot surfaces, and pinch points around the work area.

definition: Judging how likely a hazard is to cause harm and how severe the harm could be.
example: Grinding without a face shield was rated high risk due to likely eye/face injury.

definition: A safety approach that prioritizes eliminating hazards first, then engineering controls, administrative controls, and PPE last.
example: Instead of relying only on PPE, the class used welding screens and ventilation to reduce exposure.

definition: Protective gear worn to reduce exposure to hazards.
example: Students wore safety glasses, hearing protection, and gloves when cutting and grinding.

definition: Canada’s hazard communication system for workplace chemicals (labels, pictograms, SDS, training).
example: Students checked the SDS for aerosol cleaner before using it on parts.

definition: A document that explains a product’s hazards, safe handling, storage, PPE, and first aid.
example: The SDS indicated the cleaner required ventilation and nitrile gloves.

definition: A procedure to isolate energy sources so equipment cannot start during service or adjustment.
example: Before changing a cutting wheel on a powered saw, the tool was unplugged and checked for zero energy.

definition: Work that produces heat, sparks, or flames (welding, cutting, grinding).
example: A hot-work check included clearing flammables and confirming a fire extinguisher was present.

definition: Monitoring an area during and after hot work to catch smouldering fires early.
example: After grinding, the group stayed 30 minutes to ensure no sparks ignited debris under the table.

definition: Moving and removing contaminated air to reduce fume and dust exposure.
example: Local extraction was used while welding to reduce fume in the breathing zone.

definition: Metal that contains iron (often magnetic), such as steel.
example: Mild steel plate was identified as ferrous because it attracted a magnet.

definition: Metal with little or no iron, such as aluminum or copper.
example: Aluminum did not attract a magnet and required different welding settings than steel.

definition: A mixture of metals (or metal and non-metal) designed to improve properties.
example: Stainless steel is an alloy designed for corrosion resistance.

definition: Low-carbon steel that is easy to form and weld.
example: Students used 3/16-inch mild steel for practice joints because it is forgiving for beginners.

definition: The area of base metal changed by welding heat but not melted.
example: Overheating widened the HAZ and increased distortion on thin material.

definition: Unwanted bending or warping caused by uneven heating and cooling.
example: Stitch welding and alternating sides helped reduce distortion on a frame.

definition: A flexible measuring tool used for layout and cutting dimensions.
example: The cut list required verifying length twice before cutting stock.

definition: A rigid, accurate measuring tool used for short measurements and layout lines.
example: A steel rule was used to set the offset for a scribe line along an edge.

definition: A measuring tool used to measure inside, outside, and depth dimensions.
example: Calipers confirmed a drilled hole size before fitting a bolt.

definition: The allowable variation from a target dimension.
example: A hole specified at 10.00 mm ±0.10 mm must measure between 9.90 mm and 10.10 mm.

definition: A reference surface, edge, or point used to measure or locate features.
example: All hole locations were measured from the same datum edge to avoid compounding error.

definition: Marking material to guide cutting, drilling, bending, or assembly.
example: Students used a combination square and scribe to lay out a 25 mm offset line.

definition: A sharp tool used to scratch fine layout lines on metal.
example: A scribe line stayed visible after cutting fluid was applied.

definition: A tool used to make a small indentation to guide drilling.
example: A centre punch prevented the drill bit from wandering on a round surface.

definition: A technical drawing that communicates design intent, dimensions, and specifications.
example: Students used the drawing to create a cut list and a bill of materials.

definition: A drawing method showing multiple views (front/top/side) to represent a 3D object.
example: The top view clarified hole spacing that was not obvious in the front view.

definition: A 3D-looking drawing style that shows length, width, and height in one view.
example: An isometric helped the group visualise assembly order.

definition: A list of required materials, quantities, and specifications needed to build a project.
example: The BOM listed plate thickness, tubing size, and fasteners before purchasing.

definition: A list of stock pieces to cut, including dimensions and quantities.
example: The cut list reduced waste because cuts were planned around stock lengths.

definition: Tracking changes to a drawing or plan so everyone uses the correct version.
example: The group checked the revision letter before starting the final weld-up.

definition: How two pieces are arranged to be welded or fastened (lap, butt, tee, corner).
example: A tee joint was selected for the bracket because it carried load in shear and bending.

definition: How parts are aligned and held together before welding.
example: Tight fit-up reduced gaps and made it easier to control the weld puddle.

definition: A small weld used to hold parts in position before final welding.
example: Four tack welds were placed to prevent shifting during full passes.

definition: The line of deposited weld metal created by a welding pass.
example: A consistent bead width showed steady travel speed and torch angle.

definition: How deeply the weld fuses into the base metal.
example: Low penetration can fail under load even if the bead looks smooth.

definition: Proper melting and joining of the weld metal to the base metal.
example: Cold lap is poor fusion caused by low heat or incorrect technique.

definition: A triangular-shaped weld used in tee, lap, and corner joints.
example: The drawing called for a 6 mm fillet weld along the inside corner.

definition: A standardized symbol on a drawing indicating weld type, size, location, and finish.
example: The symbol specified a fillet weld on the arrow side with a specific leg size.

definition: Gas Metal Arc Welding: a wire-feed welding process using shielding gas.
example: Students used 0.030-inch wire and 75/25 shielding gas for mild steel practice.

definition: Flux-Cored Arc Welding: wire-feed welding using flux core, sometimes with shielding gas.
example: FCAW was used for outdoor work where wind can disrupt shielding gas coverage.

definition: Gas that protects the weld puddle from oxygen and nitrogen in the air.
example: 75/25 argon/CO₂ improved arc stability and reduced spatter on mild steel.

definition: Small droplets of molten metal that scatter during welding.
example: Correct voltage and stickout reduced spatter and cleanup time.

definition: Small holes in a weld caused by trapped gas or contamination.
example: Porosity increased when the base metal had oil, rust, or paint.

definition: A groove melted into the base metal along the weld toe that is not filled with weld metal.
example: Too much heat or travel speed caused undercut on the top edge of the fillet weld.

definition: Separating material to size using hand tools or powered tools.
example: Stock was rough-cut before final trimming and deburring.

definition: The width of material removed by a cutting process.
example: The cut list accounted for kerf so the final length was accurate.

definition: Removing sharp edges and burrs after cutting, drilling, or machining.
example: A deburring tool was used so parts were safe to handle and fit correctly.

definition: A rotating disc used to grind, cut, or clean metal.
example: The correct wheel type was selected for steel to avoid wheel failure.

definition: A handheld power tool that uses discs for grinding, cutting, and finishing.
example: The grinder was used to bevel edges for better weld penetration.

definition: An angled edge preparation often used before welding thicker material.
example: A bevel was ground on 3/16-inch plate to improve root fusion.

definition: Pushes or pulls that act on objects and structures.
example: A bracket experiences both tension and bending under load.

definition: A force that stretches a material.
example: A lifting strap is mainly loaded in tension.

definition: A force that squeezes a material.
example: A column in a frame carries compression from the load above.

definition: A force that causes parts of a material to slide past each other.
example: Bolts in a lap joint often carry shear forces.

definition: A turning effect that causes a member to bend.
example: A longer lever arm increases bending moment on the mount.

definition: A design margin that makes a structure stronger than the expected maximum load.
example: The project used a factor of safety to account for unknowns and wear over time.

definition: A mechanical device used to join parts (bolts, screws, rivets).
example: Fasteners were chosen where the assembly may need to be disassembled later.

definition: A twisting force used to tighten fasteners to a specification.
example: Bolts were tightened in stages to the specified torque to prevent distortion.

definition: The distance between threads on a fastener (or threads per inch in imperial).
example: The nut would not start because the thread pitch did not match the bolt.

definition: Testing that damages or breaks a sample to evaluate performance.
example: A bend test was used on a weld coupon to check for cracking and lack of fusion.

definition: Testing that evaluates a part without damaging it.
example: A visual inspection and dye penetrant check were used to find surface cracks.

definition: Checking a part or weld with the eyes (often with gauges) for defects and standards.
example: The weld was inspected for undercut, porosity, and consistent bead shape.

definition: The set of requirements a part must meet to be considered acceptable.
example: The rubric specified allowable porosity and minimum weld size as acceptance criteria.

definition: Organizing tasks, materials, time, and safety steps before starting work.
example: Students planned the build sequence: cut, prep, tack, weld, clean, inspect, finish.

definition: The order of steps used to complete a job safely and efficiently.
example: The work sequence placed drilling before welding to keep parts easy to clamp.

definition: Preventing defects by using standards, checks, and good process control.
example: QA included measuring after each step so errors were caught early.

definition: Finding defects by inspecting and testing finished work against requirements.
example: QC included checking dimensions and inspecting welds before final sign-off.

definition: Meeting workplace expectations: safety, punctuality, respect, and accountability.
example: A student reported a near miss, cleaned the station, and logged the issue appropriately.

definition: Tracking tools so they are returned, maintained, and ready for the next user.
example: Students checked tools in/out and reported damaged items immediately.

definition: Keeping a clean, organized, and hazard-free workspace.
example: Grinding dust was cleaned up to reduce slip and fire hazards.
